sections.title: Pedunculate oak
sections.text: Quercus robur is a large deciduous oak native across much of Europe and parts of western Asia. It commonly reaches 20–40 m and develops a broad crown. Its leaves have deep rounded lobes and a short stalk; the acorns sit in cups on conspicuously long stalks.

sections.title: Acorns and comparison
sections.text: Acorns are about 2–3 cm long and have been eaten after processing, including grinding into flour. They are rich in bitter tannins, so they require leaching or other preparation; raw or inadequately prepared acorns are not a ready-to-eat food. Unlike evergreen holm oak (Q. ilex), this species sheds its leaves; it also differs from the downy oak and northern red oak in its long-stalked acorns.
